firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Hi Kaggle & Gemma Community! 👋

 As part of our submission for the **Google – The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track** (targeting *Overall Best Paper* & *Best New Resource & Application*), we are open-sourcing our deterministic pre-flight verification and code slicing suite designed specifically for running software engineering agents on local /  edge-tier Gemma 4 models (e.g., `gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct`).

 ### 🎯 The Challenge: Context Saturation & Syntax Regressions in 24GB VRAM
 When deploying SWE agents on a single NVIDIA L4 (24GB VRAM), agents quickly encounter two catastrophic failure modes:
  1. **Context Window Exhaustion:** Full file reading and 500+ line uncompressed Pytest failure tracebacks saturate the attention window, triggering context compression degradation and token quota blowups.
  2. **First-Pass Syntax Regressions:** In multi-turn self-correction loops, small model patches frequently introduce trivial indentation errors, unclosed
 brackets, or invalid syntax, wasting precious container execution cycles.

    ---
    
    ### 🛠 The Solution: AST-Guided Verification Suite (Apache 2.0)
    We developed a lightweight, zero-external-dependency deterministic verification suite that acts as an OS-level syntax gate and context filter before invoking
    the model or spinning up containers:
    
    1. **AST-Guided Deterministic Code Slicing:** Extracts exact function/class hierarchies and target line ranges via Python's `ast` module, reducing context
    prompt volume by **44.6%** compared to full-file dumps.
    2. **Sub-Millisecond Pre-Flight Syntax Gate:** Validates AST tree integrity in **47.2 µs** (measured on Kaggle CPU) before dispatching edits, preventing broken
    patches from ever entering container execution.
    3. **Lossless Pytest Traceback Compressor:** Isolates the root cause (`FAILURES` / `ERRORS` block and chained exceptions) while deterministically trimming
    boilerplate setup lines, yielding **30.6% log compression** with zero root-cause loss.
    
    ---
    
    ### 🔬 Empirical Benchmarks (Verified on Kaggle Cloud Kernel)
    All metrics are deterministically reproducible in our public kernel (31/31 unit tests pass in 3.25 ms):
    
    | Component / Metric | Raw Baseline | AST-Guided Suite | Impact / Speedup |
    | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
    | **Code Slicing Prompt Volume** | Full Module Dump | Target AST Slice | **-44.6% tokens** |
    | **Syntax Gate Latency** | Full Lint Pipeline | `ast.parse` Gate | **47.2 µs** |
    | **Traceback Size (Pytest Log)** | 75 Lines | 52 Lines (Root Cause Preserved) | **-30.6% tokens** |
    | **Cloud Test Suite Runtime** | — | 31/31 Unit Tests Passing | **3.25 ms** |
    
    ---

    ### 📋 Pre-Registration Notice & Methodology
    In adherence to rigorous scientific practices, our full 10-task paired SWE-bench Lite pilot evaluation protocol comparing baseline Gemma 4 vs. AST-augmented
    Gemma 4 has been pre-registered:
    - **E2E Protocol Document:** `PROTOCOL_E2E_GEMMA.md` (Git commit `46b2907`)
    - **Model Checkpoint:** `google/gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct`
    - **Statistical Framework:** Exact paired two-tailed test with fixed token budgets and deterministic temperature ($T=0.0$).

    ---

    ### 🔗 Open-Source Community Links
    - 💻 **Public Executable Notebook:** [AST-Guided Loops Verification for Gemma 4
    (v13)](https://www.kaggle.com/code/msingatullin/ast-guided-loops-verification-for-gemma-4)
    - 🐙 **GitHub Repository:** https://github.com/msingatullin/gemma-4-developer-agent (Apache 2.0)
    - 📄 **Official Kaggle Writeup:** [AST-Guided Loops: Deterministic Verification for Gemma 4 SWE
    Agents](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent-paper/writeups/ast-guided-deterministic-gemma4-agent)

    We welcome community feedback, testing on your own agent loops, and suggestions for additional AST transformations! If this open-source utility helps your
    Gemma 4 agent development, an upvote or star is greatly appreciated! 🚀
